metadata.title: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health
metadata.version: Edn. presented at the EAU Annual Congress, Madrid 2025
metadata.specialty: Urology and sexual and reproductive health
metadata.summary: The available chapters address the definition, causes, diagnostic evaluation and management of male infertility, including genetic conditions, reproductive tract disorders and fertility preservation in men with cancer. They examine non-invasive treatments, surgical sperm retrieval and assisted reproductive technologies, while distinguishing established recommendations from interventions with limited evidence. The material also discusses psychosocial effects, long-term health risks and survivorship in male sexual and reproductive health.

conditions_covered: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD)
Congenital unilateral absence of the vas deferens (CUAVD)
target_population: Men in couples seeking help for infertility
Female partners of men undergoing infertility evaluation
Men with testicular cancer or receiving gonadotoxic treatment
Men with sexual and reproductive health concerns
therapeutic_areas: Transurethral resection of the ejaculatory ducts (TURED)

toxicities.incidence: Vascular injury can cause testicular atrophy in 1-2% of cases; post-operative atrophy was 12% in men with non-palpable testes and long vascular pedicles permitting scrotal placement, and has been reported in up to 40% of patients after staged orchidopexy.

toxicities.event: Impaired fertility after treatment for testicular germ cell tumour
recognition: Sperm aneuploidy up to two years following gonadotoxic therapy
DNA damage and increased SDF after chemotherapy
prevention: Offer sperm cryopreservation before planned orchidectomy or other gonadotoxic or ablative treatment.
Offer onco-TESE during radical orchidectomy to men with testicular cancer and azoospermia or severe semen abnormalities.
Use contraception throughout treatment and for at least six months after its completion.

toxicities.event: Hypogonadism, sexual dysfunction and cardiovascular disease after treatment for testicular germ cell tumour

management.severity: Persistent signs or symptoms of testosterone deficiency
management.actions: Consider delaying testosterone therapy until deficiency remains clinically apparent; account for its potential to worsen spermatogenesis when fertility is a priority.

prevention: Provide multidisciplinary follow-up through a dedicated late-effects clinic and survivorship programme.
Do not use testosterone therapy to treat male infertility.
In men treated for TGCT who prioritise fertility, weigh treatment of testosterone-deficiency symptoms against deterioration in spermatogenesis.

recognition: Coil displacement or migration to the femoral vein or right atrium

toxicities.event: Complications of scrotal operation for varicocele
recognition: Arterial injury with possible devascularisation and testicular gangrene
Pain after incision of the external oblique fascia

toxicities.event: Complications of open retroperitoneal high ligation
recognition: Failure to ligate the external spermatic vein

toxicities.event: Complications of microsurgical inguinal or Subinguinal varicocele surgery

recognition: Failure to ligate the external spermatic vein
Post-operative right shoulder pain associated with diaphragmatic stretching during pneumo-peritoneum

toxicities.event: Complications of transurethral resection of the ejaculatory ducts
recognition: Azoospermia in cases of partial distal ejaculatory duct obstruction
Urine reflux into the ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles

toxicities.event: Bleeding, scrotal haematoma and post-operative pain after testicular sperm aspiration
Intratesticular haematoma and testicular fibrosis after conventional testicular sperm extraction
toxicities.incidence: Intratesticular haematoma was detected by scrotal US in 51.7% of patients 3 months after surgery; testicular fibrosis was observed in up to 30% of patients at 6-months’ assessment. The longer-term functional significance remains unclear.

toxicities.event: Post-operative decline in testosterone after testicular sperm extraction
toxicities.incidence: A meta-analysis found a mean 2.7 nmol/L decline in total testosterone 6 months after cTESE in patients with NOA, with recovery to baseline within 18-26 months.
prevention: Consider long-term endocrine follow-up after TESE, regardless of technique, to identify hypogonadism.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Offer sperm cryopreservation before planned orchidectomy or gonadotoxic or ablative cancer treatment. Offer onco-TESE during radical orchidectomy when testicular cancer is accompanied by azoospermia or severe semen abnormalities.
prophylaxis.target_population: Men with cancer whose planned treatment may impair spermatogenesis or ejaculation
prophylaxis.duration: Before planned orchidectomy or other gonadotoxic or ablative treatment; onco-TESE at radical orchidectomy

prophylaxis.recommendation: Use contraception because chemotherapy and RT are teratogenic.
prophylaxis.duration: During treatment and for at least six months after completion

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise regular testicular self-examination because of increased testicular-cancer risk.
prophylaxis.target_population: Men with a history of cryptorchidism

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise self-examination even when no additional risk factors are present, to facilitate early detection of TGCT.

prophylaxis.type: Prevention of sexually transmitted infection transmission
prophylaxis.recommendation: Refer sexual partners for evaluation and treatment when the patient's accessory sex gland infection is known or suspected to result from a sexually transmitted disease.

infection_management.management: Treat the infection; sperm quality may improve, but an increased probability of conception does not necessarily follow. In suspected genitourinary infection, perform semen culture or PCR for common urinary tract pathogens. Antibiotic treatment may eradicate organisms without reversing functional deficits or anatomical abnormalities.
Antibiotic therapy has provided symptom relief, microbial eradication and reductions in cellular and humoral inflammatory findings in urogenital secretions.
Antibiotics might improve sperm quality, but there is no evidence that treatment increases the likelihood of natural conception.

Confirm leukocytospermia with a semen peroxidase test. There is no evidence that treating leukocytospermia alone improves conception rates; evidence is insufficient to determine whether antibiotics or antioxidants improve fertility outcomes in infertile men with this finding.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Epididymitis caused or suspected to be caused by N. gonorrhoeae or C. trachomatis
infection_management.prevention: Advise patients to refer their sexual partners for evaluation and treatment to help prevent transmission.
infection_management.management: Treat epididymitis to eradicate infection, improve symptoms and reduce potential testicular damage and complications. Advise patients to refer their sexual partners for evaluation and treatment.
During follow-up, consider possible epididymal-duct stenosis, reduced sperm count and azoospermia.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Asymptomatic C. trachomatis or M. hominis in semen
infection_management.management: Sperm-quality impairment may improve after antibiotic treatment, but further research is needed to confirm this finding.
Treatment is not always recommended. The document notes that interpretation of mycoplasma findings in ejaculate is complicated by normal urethral colonisation.
Associations with infertility and poorer pregnancy outcomes require prospective validation before their clinical implications can be clearly established.
Whether antiviral therapy improves fertility rates is unclear.

therapies_index.name: ART
approved_indications: Fertility treatment when the couple’s circumstances favour assisted reproduction over surgical intervention.

therapies_index.name: ICSI
therapies_index.mechanism: An oocyte and sperm are handled in vitro to establish pregnancy.
approved_indications: Treatment using surgically retrieved sperm in obstructive or non-obstructive azoospermia.
Treatment using sperm retrieved in men with CBAVD or CF.

therapies_index.name: IVF
therapies_index.mechanism: Oocytes and sperm, or embryos, are handled in vitro with the aim of establishing pregnancy.
approved_indications: Fertility treatment, including treatment following sperm retrieval.

therapies_index.name: IUI
approved_indications: Assisted reproduction discussed in relation to sperm DNA fragmentation and varicocele treatment.

therapies_index.name: TESE
therapies_index.mechanism: Sperm are retrieved directly from testicular tissue.
approved_indications: Sperm retrieval for ICSI in selected men with azoospermia or obstruction.
Possible case-by-case use after ART failure in men with unexplained infertility and elevated SDF; the evidence is limited.
Sperm retrieval during reconstructive surgery when reconstruction is impossible.
key_toxicities: Intratesticular haematoma, testicular fibrosis and a temporary reduction in testosterone have been reported after conventional TESE.
monitoring: Consider long-term endocrine follow-up to detect hypogonadism.

therapies_index.name: mTESE
therapies_index.mechanism: An operative microscope is used to identify seminiferous tubules more likely to contain sperm while limiting tissue removal.
approved_indications: The preferred surgical sperm-retrieval approach for men with NOA.
Sperm retrieval in selected men with azoospermia and Klinefelter syndrome.
Possible salvage sperm retrieval after an unsuccessful earlier retrieval procedure.
therapies_index.administration: The tubules are inspected under an operative microscope at 20-25x magnification.
key_toxicities: Haematoma and fibrosis can occur, although reported rates are lower than with cTESE.
monitoring: Consider long-term endocrine follow-up to detect hypogonadism.

therapies_index.name: onco-TESE
therapies_index.mechanism: Testicular sperm are retrieved for fertility preservation during oncological surgery.
approved_indications: Offer at radical orchidectomy to men with testicular cancer and azoospermia or severe semen-parameter abnormalities.
therapies_index.administration: Performed at the time of radical orchidectomy.

therapies_index.name: MESA
therapies_index.mechanism: Sperm are collected microsurgically from the epididymis.
approved_indications: Sperm retrieval in men with CBAVD or other epididymal obstruction.
Sperm retrieval during reconstructive surgery when reconstruction is impossible, or as an alternative when repair is unsuitable.

therapies_index.name: PESA
therapies_index.mechanism: Sperm are aspirated percutaneously from the epididymis.
approved_indications: Sperm retrieval in men with CBAVD or other obstruction when indicated for ICSI.

therapies_index.name: TESA
therapies_index.mechanism: Testicular tissue is aspirated with a biopsy needle.
approved_indications: A sperm-retrieval option in obstructive azoospermia; it is not recommended for patients with NOA.
therapies_index.administration: An office-based procedure performed under local anaesthesia.
key_toxicities: Minor bleeding, scrotal haematoma and postoperative pain.

therapies_index.name: FNA mapping
therapies_index.mechanism: Testicular tissue obtained by needle aspiration is evaluated to locate areas more likely to yield sperm.
key_toxicities: A subsequent invasive retrieval procedure may increase the risk of testicular damage.

therapies_index.name: proximal vas deferens sperm aspiration
therapies_index.mechanism: Sperm are aspirated from the proximal vas deferens.
approved_indications: Sperm retrieval for future ICSI when an inguinal vas deferens defect cannot be repaired.
An alternative sperm-retrieval approach in ejaculatory duct obstruction.

therapies_index.name: seminal vesicle-ultrasonically guided aspiration
approved_indications: An alternative sperm-retrieval approach in ejaculatory duct obstruction.

therapies_index.name: sperm cryopreservation
therapies_index.mechanism: Collected sperm are preserved for later fertility treatment.
approved_indications: Fertility preservation before gonadotoxic cancer treatment or surgery that may impair sperm production or ejaculation.
Fertility preservation before planned orchidectomy.
Preservation of sperm retrieved during surgery for subsequent ICSI.
therapies_index.administration: Offer before planned orchidectomy or other gonadotoxic oncological treatment; surgically retrieved sperm may be preserved during an operation.

therapies_index.name: orchidopexy
therapies_index.mechanism: An undescended testis is surgically positioned to preserve testicular function where feasible.
approved_indications: May be offered to adults with an undescended testis and biochemical hypogonadism or impaired sperm production.
May be considered for bilateral cryptorchidism when fertility preservation is valued.
therapies_index.administration: When correcting an undescended testis in adulthood, perform a simultaneous biopsy to assess for GCNIS.
key_toxicities: Vascular injury may cause testicular atrophy in 1-2% of cases; postoperative atrophy was reported in 12% of non-palpable testes with long vascular pedicles and in up to 40% after staged orchidopexy.

therapies_index.name: orchidectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: The testis is surgically removed.
approved_indications: Offer to adults with a unilateral undescended testis and normal hormonal function or spermatogenesis.
May be recommended in adolescence for an intra-abdominal testis when the contralateral testis is normal.
An option after multidisciplinary assessment of a suspicious testicular lesion.
key_toxicities: Treatment of TGCT, including orchidectomy, may adversely affect reproductive function.

therapies_index.name: radical orchidectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: The affected testis is surgically removed.
approved_indications: A treatment option for a suspicious or indeterminate testicular lesion after counselling and multidisciplinary discussion.
key_toxicities: May adversely affect reproductive function.
monitoring: Arrange sperm cryopreservation beforehand when feasible; offer onco-TESE during surgery to men with testicular cancer and azoospermia or severe semen abnormalities.

therapies_index.name: testicular biopsy
therapies_index.mechanism: Testicular tissue is sampled for histological assessment.
approved_indications: Perform alongside correction of an undescended testis in adulthood to detect GCNIS.
Offer to selected infertile men with TM and additional risk factors.
May be considered for a suspicious or enlarging testicular lesion after multidisciplinary discussion.
key_toxicities: The risks and complications of biopsy should be discussed when it is considered for TM-related cancer risk.

therapies_index.name: US-guided biopsy with intra-operative frozen section analysis
therapies_index.mechanism: An ultrasound-guided tissue sample is assessed during surgery to help characterise an indeterminate testicular lesion.
approved_indications: May be offered as an alternative to radical orchidectomy after counselling and multidisciplinary discussion of an indeterminate testicular lesion.

therapies_index.name: varicocele repair
approved_indications: Treat infertile men with clinical varicocele, abnormal semen parameters and otherwise unexplained infertility when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
May be considered for elevated SDF with otherwise unexplained infertility or ART failure after counselling.
Offer surgery to adolescents with a persistently small testis meeting the specified size-difference criteria.
key_toxicities: Recurrence, hydrocele and other procedure-dependent complications are reported.
monitoring: In adolescents, confirm a testicular size difference of > 2 mL or 20% at two subsequent visits six months apart.

therapies_index.name: varicocelectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Surgical correction of a varicocele.
approved_indications: Clinical varicocele with abnormal semen parameters in appropriately selected infertile men.
May be considered in selected men with elevated SDF or hypogonadism, with counselling about limitations of the evidence.
key_toxicities: Recurrence and hydrocele are reported; complication rates vary by technique.
monitoring: Semen-parameter improvement may take up to two spermatogenic cycles.

therapies_index.name: microsurgical subinguinal varicocelectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: A varicocele is repaired through a microsurgical subinguinal approach.
approved_indications: Surgical treatment of an appropriately selected clinical varicocele.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele and scrotal haematoma are reported for the microsurgical inguinal or subinguinal approach.

therapies_index.name: robot-assisted varicocelectomy
approved_indications: A described surgical approach to varicocele treatment; larger prospective randomised studies are needed.

therapies_index.name: antegrade sclerotherapy
approved_indications: Treatment of varicocele.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele (5.5%), haematoma, infection, scrotal pain, testicular atrophy, epididymitis, technical failure 1-9% and left-flank erythema.

therapies_index.name: retrograde sclerotherapy
approved_indications: Treatment of varicocele.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele (3.3%), wound infection, scrotal pain, technical failure 6-7.5%, adverse reaction to contrast medium, flank pain, persistent thrombophlebitis and venous perforation.

therapies_index.name: retrograde embolization
approved_indications: Treatment of varicocele.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele (10%), haematoma, wound infection, technical failure 7-27%, thrombophlebitis-related pain, contrast-media reactions, coil misplacement or migration, retroperitoneal haemorrhage, fibrosis, ureteric obstruction and venous perforation.

therapies_index.name: scrotal operation
approved_indications: A listed open surgical approach to varicocele treatment.
key_toxicities: Testicular atrophy, arterial injury with possible devascularisation and testicular gangrene, scrotal haematoma and postoperative hydrocele.

therapies_index.name: inguinal approach
approved_indications: A listed surgical approach to varicocele treatment.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele (7.3%), testicular atrophy, epididymo-orchitis, wound complications, postoperative pain and genitofemoral nerve damage.

therapies_index.name: open retroperitoneal high ligation
approved_indications: Treatment of varicocele.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele (5-10%), testicular atrophy, scrotal oedema and failure to ligate the external spermatic vein.

therapies_index.name: laparoscopy
approved_indications: A listed approach to varicocele treatment.
key_toxicities: Hydrocele (7-43%), epididymitis, wound infection, testicular atrophy following arterial injury, bleeding, injury to bowel, vessels or nerves, pulmonary embolism, pneumo-scrotum, peritonitis and postoperative shoulder pain.

therapies_index.name: EV
therapies_index.mechanism: Microsurgical reconstruction connects the epididymis and vas deferens to restore passage of sperm.
approved_indications: Acquired epididymal obstruction when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
May be indicated during vasectomy reversal if findings suggest secondary epididymal obstruction.
therapies_index.administration: Sperm retrieval and cryopreservation should be performed during surgery if reconstruction proves impossible.
key_toxicities: Late failure is reported.
monitoring: Assess postoperative patency; recanalisation may take 3-18 months.

therapies_index.name: microsurgical vasovasostomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Microsurgical reconstruction restores continuity of the vas deferens.
approved_indications: Azoospermia due to vasal obstruction when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
Reversal of vas deferens obstruction after vasectomy.
key_toxicities: Late failure is reported but uncommon.

therapies_index.name: robot-assisted vasovasostomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Robot-assisted reconstruction restores continuity of the vas deferens.
approved_indications: A described approach to vasectomy reversal; larger studies are needed to establish its benefits over standard microsurgery.

therapies_index.name: robot-assisted EV
therapies_index.mechanism: Robot-assisted reconstruction joins the epididymis and vas deferens.
approved_indications: A described approach to epididymal obstruction; larger studies are needed.

therapies_index.name: TURED
therapies_index.mechanism: The ejaculatory ducts are resected transurethrally to relieve obstruction.
approved_indications: Post-inflammatory or cystic ejaculatory duct obstruction.
key_toxicities: Epididymitis, UTI, gross haematuria, haematospermia, azoospermia in partial distal obstruction and urinary reflux into the ejaculatory ducts or seminal vesicles.

therapies_index.name: seminal vesiculoscopy
therapies_index.mechanism: Debris or calculi are removed from the seminal vesicle.
approved_indications: An alternative treatment for ejaculatory duct obstruction.

therapies_index.name: balloon dilation
approved_indications: An alternative treatment for ejaculatory duct obstruction.

therapies_index.name: laser incision
approved_indications: An alternative treatment for ejaculatory duct obstruction involving calcification seen on TRUS.

therapies_index.name: hCG
therapies_index.mechanism: Acts like LH to stimulate intratesticular testosterone production and spermatogenesis after puberty.
approved_indications: Induction of spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.
Post-pubertal secondary hypogonadism, initially alone or with FSH.
May be considered after persistent infertility following withdrawal of anabolic steroids.
therapies_index.administration: For post-pubertal onset, the suggested starting dose is 250 IU hCG twice weekly; if testosterone reaches normal levels, the dose may be increased up to 2,000 IU twice weekly.
key_toxicities: hCG treatment for cryptorchidism has been reported to be potentially harmful to future spermatogenesis.
monitoring: During treatment for post-pubertal secondary hypogonadism, perform semen analysis every 3 months unless conception occurs.
Assess testosterone levels when adjusting the dose.

therapies_index.name: FSH
therapies_index.mechanism: Promotes spermatogenesis and testicular growth during puberty.
approved_indications: Use to increase spermatogenesis in men with idiopathic oligozoospermia and FSH values within the normal range.
Use with hCG to induce spermatogenesis in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; it may be added after an inadequate response to hCG or started in combination.
therapies_index.administration: When added after hCG in post-pubertal secondary hypogonadism, 75 IU three times per week, increasing to 150 IU three times per week if indicated.
monitoring: During treatment for post-pubertal secondary hypogonadism, perform semen analysis every 3 months unless conception occurs.

therapies_index.name: hCG and FSH
therapies_index.mechanism: Combines stimulation of intratesticular testosterone production with stimulation of spermatogenesis.
approved_indications: Induction of spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; the agents may be combined from the beginning of treatment or used sequentially.
therapies_index.administration: For post-pubertal onset, the described hCG starting dose is 250 IU hCG twice weekly, potentially increasing up to 2,000 IU twice weekly; FSH may be given at 75 IU three times per week, increasing to 150 IU three times per week if indicated.
monitoring: Perform semen analysis every 3 months unless conception occurs.
Assess testosterone levels when adjusting hCG.

therapies_index.name: human menopausal gonadotropins
approved_indications: Drug therapy to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.

therapies_index.name: recombinant FSH
therapies_index.mechanism: FSH promotes spermatogenesis and testicular growth.
approved_indications: Drug therapy to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.

therapies_index.name: highly purified FSH
therapies_index.mechanism: FSH promotes spermatogenesis and testicular growth.
approved_indications: Drug therapy to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.

therapies_index.name: pulsatile GnRH
approved_indications: An option described for prepubertal secondary hypogonadism, although administration is difficult.
therapies_index.administration: Pulsatile administration; no dose is given.

therapies_index.name: GnRH analogues
approved_indications: The cited paediatric guidance recommends endocrine treatment with GnRH analogues for boys with bilateral undescended testis; endocrine treatment is not recommended routinely to achieve testicular descent, and hormonal treatment is not recommended for post-pubertal cryptorchidism.

therapies_index.name: testosterone therapy
approved_indications: Symptomatic primary or secondary hypogonadism in men not considering parenthood.
May be considered for Klinefelter syndrome after fertility issues are addressed if testosterone levels are in the hypogonadal range.
It must not be used to treat male infertility.
key_toxicities: May worsen spermatogenesis when fertility is being pursued.
Men with Klinefelter syndrome have elevated metabolic and cardiovascular risks, including VTE and diabetes, particularly when starting testosterone therapy.
monitoring: In patients treated for TGCT, consider delaying initiation until signs or symptoms of testosterone deficiency are persistent.

therapies_index.name: dopamine agonist therapy
approved_indications: Proven hyperprolactinaemia associated with reduced fertility, to improve sperm quality.

therapies_index.name: bromocriptine
approved_indications: Named as a dopamine agonist used for hyperprolactinaemia.

therapies_index.name: cabergoline
approved_indications: Named as a dopamine agonist used for hyperprolactinaemia.

therapies_index.name: quinagolide
approved_indications: Named as a dopamine agonist used for hyperprolactinaemia.

therapies_index.name: SERMs
therapies_index.mechanism: Block hypothalamic oestrogen receptors, increasing GnRH and pituitary gonadotropin secretion and stimulating spermatogenesis.
approved_indications: Discussed as an off-label possibility for selected fertility-conscious men treated for TGCT and as an option after persistent infertility following withdrawal of anabolic steroids.
Routine use for idiopathic infertility is not recommended because the evidence is inconclusive.
key_toxicities: Complications were under-reported in studies of idiopathic infertility.

therapies_index.name: clomiphene
approved_indications: An off-label option discussed for fertility-conscious men treated for TGCT.
An option discussed if infertility persists after withdrawal of anabolic steroids.

therapies_index.name: AIs
therapies_index.mechanism: Reduce oestrogen production by inhibiting aromatase and its negative feedback on the hypothalamus, promoting gonadotropin secretion.
approved_indications: Described as an off-label option in infertility with testicular dysfunction and low serum testosterone and/or a low testosterone-to-oestradiol ratio.
Routine use for idiopathic infertility is not recommended because evidence is inconclusive.

therapies_index.name: testolactone
therapies_index.mechanism: As an aromatase inhibitor, reduces conversion of androgens to oestrogens.
approved_indications: Named as a steroidal aromatase inhibitor studied in infertile men; routine treatment of idiopathic infertility is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: anastrozole
therapies_index.mechanism: As an aromatase inhibitor, reduces conversion of androgens to oestrogens.
approved_indications: Named as a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor studied in infertile men; routine treatment of idiopathic infertility is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: letrozole
therapies_index.mechanism: As an aromatase inhibitor, reduces conversion of androgens to oestrogens.
approved_indications: Named as a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor studied in infertile men; routine treatment of idiopathic infertility is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: antioxidant therapy
approved_indications: Studied for male infertility, but routine treatment of idiopathic infertility is not recommended because the evidence is inconclusive.

therapies_index.name: prebiotic/probiotic supplementation
therapies_index.mechanism: May influence hormone secretion, facilitate free-radical removal and improve the prostatic microenvironment, indirectly supporting sperm function.
approved_indications: Studied in idiopathic infertility and after varicocelectomy; routine use for idiopathic infertility is not recommended because the evidence is inconclusive.

therapies_index.name: antibiotic therapy
approved_indications: Treatment of male accessory gland infections may improve sperm quality without necessarily improving conception probability.
Chronic bacterial prostatitis: treatment has provided symptom relief, microbial eradication and reductions in inflammatory parameters.
monitoring: Assess clinical symptoms and microbiological response when treating chronic bacterial prostatitis.

therapies_index.name: weight loss
approved_indications: Lifestyle improvement advised for infertile men to improve their chances of conception; it may also improve obesity-related secondary hypogonadism.

therapies_index.name: physical activity
approved_indications: Lifestyle improvement advised for infertile men to improve their chances of conception.

therapies_index.name: smoking cessation
approved_indications: Lifestyle improvement advised for infertile men to improve their chances of conception.

therapies_index.name: alcohol intake reduction
approved_indications: Lifestyle improvement advised for infertile men to improve their chances of conception.

therapies_index.name: chemotherapy
approved_indications: Oncological treatment discussed in relation to fertility preservation and survivorship.
key_toxicities: Teratogenicity, impaired fertility, potentially cumulative-dose-dependent long-term infertility, sperm DNA damage and increased SDF are reported.
monitoring: Use contraception during treatment and for at least six months after completion.

therapies_index.name: radiotherapy
approved_indications: Oncological treatment discussed in relation to fertility preservation and survivorship.
key_toxicities: Teratogenicity and impaired fertility are reported; long-term infertility after RT is described as rare.
monitoring: Use contraception during treatment and for at least six months after completion.

therapies_index.name: psychological support
approved_indications: Support for men experiencing infertility-related distress, including prolonged grief after unsuccessful treatment.
therapies_index.administration: May range from psycho-education to more comprehensive psycho-therapeutic approaches across stages of infertility care.

recommendations.statement: Evaluate a couple for infertility after twelve consecutive months of regular intercourse without contraception and no conception.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.2.2 Summary of evidence and recommendations on epidemiology and aetiology of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Assess both partners at the same time to establish the cause of infertility.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.2.2 Summary of evidence and recommendations on epidemiology and aetiology of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Evaluate every man in a couple seeking medical assistance for fertility difficulties.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.2.2 Summary of evidence and recommendations on epidemiology and aetiology of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Assess the female partner’s fertility, including ovarian reserve, alongside diagnosis and management of the infertile man.
recommendations.context: The female partner’s findings may affect treatment timing and the choice between ART and surgery.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Examine every man who seeks medical care for fertility difficulties, including those with abnormal semen parameters.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Obtain a thorough medical, reproductive and family history; assess lifestyle and behavioural risks; perform a physical examination and semen analysis.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Counsel infertile men and men with abnormal semen parameters about associated health risks.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Measure testicular volume using Prader’s orchidometer or testicular ultrasound (US).
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Conduct semen analyses in accordance with the most recent edition of the WHO Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: If the initial semen analysis is abnormal, obtain at least two consecutive semen analyses.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Do not use reactive oxygen species (ROS) testing routinely when diagnosing or managing the male partner of an infertile couple.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Test sperm DNA fragmentation (SDF) when assessing couples with recurrent pregnancy loss after natural conception or ART failure, or men with unexplained infertility.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Consider testicular sperm for intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) in patients whose ejaculated sperm has high SDF, while treating this approach as experimental.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: At a minimum, measure serum total testosterone and Follicle Stimulating Hormone/Luteinising Hormone in every man with oligozoospermia or azoospermia.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Offer standard karyotype testing and genetic counselling for diagnostic purposes to all men with azoospermia or oligozoospermia with spermatozoa < 5 million/mL.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Provide men with Klinefelter syndrome with long-term endocrine follow-up and appropriate medical treatment.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Test for Y-chromosome microdeletions when sperm concentration is ≤ 1 million sperm/mL; consider testing when it is < 5 million sperm/mL.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Tell men with Yq microdeletion and their partners who intend to use ICSI that sons will inherit the microdeletion.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Do not perform testicular sperm extraction when complete deletions include the AZFa and AZFb regions.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Test men with structural vas deferens abnormalities—unilateral or bilateral absence without renal anomalies—and their partners for cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene mutations.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Provide genetic counselling to every couple in whom a clinical or genetic assessment identifies a genetic abnormality, and to patients carrying a potentially heritable disease.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Perform scrotal US in patients with infertility.
recommendations.rationale: Infertile men have an increased risk of testis cancer.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: In a multidisciplinary team, discuss invasive diagnostic options for infertile men with indeterminate testicular lesions detected by US, particularly when additional malignancy risk factors are present; options include US-guided biopsy with frozen section, radical orchidectomy and surveillance.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Perform transrectal US when partial or complete distal obstruction is suspected.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.3.7 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the diagnostic work-up of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Do not use hormonal treatment for cryptorchidism in post-pubertal men.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.1.3 Summary of evidence recommendations for cryptorchidism

recommendations.statement: When correcting undescended testes in adulthood, perform a concurrent testicular biopsy to detect intratubular germ cell neoplasia in situ, formerly carcinoma in situ.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.1.3 Summary of evidence recommendations for cryptorchidism

recommendations.statement: Offer orchidectomy to adult men with a unilateral undescended testis who have normal hormonal function and spermatogenesis.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.1.3 Summary of evidence recommendations for cryptorchidism

recommendations.statement: If technically feasible, offer unilateral or bilateral orchidopexy to adult men with unilateral or bilateral undescended testes and biochemical hypogonadism and/or spermatogenic failure.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.1.3 Summary of evidence recommendations for cryptorchidism

recommendations.statement: Advise men with testicular microcalcification (TM) to examine their testes themselves, even if no other risk factors are present.
recommendations.rationale: Self-examination may enable earlier detection of a testicular germ cell tumour (TGCT).
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: For isolated TM without associated risk factors, do not perform testicular biopsy, follow-up scrotal ultrasound (US), biochemical tumour-marker measurement, or abdominal or pelvic computed tomography.
recommendations.context: Associated risk factors listed are infertility, cryptorchidism, testicular cancer and atrophic testis.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: Offer testicular biopsy to infertile men with TM who have spermatogenic failure, bilateral TM, atrophic testes (< 12 mL), a history of undescended testes or a history of TGCT.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: When a patient with TM and an associated lesion has suspicious findings on examination or US, undertake inguinal surgical exploration with testicular biopsy or offer orchidectomy after multidisciplinary team review and discussion with the patient.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: Manage men previously treated for TGCT through a multidisciplinary team with a dedicated late-effects clinic and survivorship programme.
recommendations.rationale: These men face increased risks of hypogonadism, sexual dysfunction and cardiovascular problems.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: Cryopreserve sperm before a planned orchidectomy or before further neoadjuvant or adjuvant cancer treatment.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: At radical orchidectomy, offer onco-testicular sperm extraction (onco-TESE) to men with testicular cancer who have azoospermia or severe semen-parameter abnormalities.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.2.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for germ cell malignancy and testicular microcalcification

recommendations.statement: Offer varicocele surgery to adolescents with a persistently small testis showing a size difference of > 2 mL or 20%, confirmed at two subsequent visits six months apart.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for varicocele

recommendations.statement: Do not treat a varicocele in an infertile man whose semen analysis is normal or in a man with a sub-clinical varicocele.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for varicocele

recommendations.statement: Treat infertile men who have a clinical varicocele and abnormal semen parameters when the couple’s infertility is otherwise unexplained and the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
recommendations.rationale: The recommended treatment aims to improve fertility rates.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for varicocele

recommendations.statement: Consider varicocelectomy for men with raised sperm DNA fragmentation and otherwise unexplained infertility, or after failure of assisted reproductive techniques, including recurrent pregnancy loss or failure of embryogenesis or implantation.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for varicocele

recommendations.statement: Treat male accessory gland infections, recognising that sperm quality may improve but conception does not necessarily become more likely.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.4.4 Summary of evidence and recommendation for male accessory gland infections

recommendations.statement: Refer the sexual partners of patients whose accessory sex gland infections are known or suspected to result from sexually transmitted diseases for evaluation and treatment.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.4.4.4 Summary of evidence and recommendation for male accessory gland infections

recommendations.statement: Explain to infertile men the adverse effects of obesity, insufficient physical activity, smoking and high alcohol intake on sperm quality and testosterone levels, and advise improvements in these lifestyle factors to increase the chance of conception.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.2 Summary of evidence and recommendation for Non-Invasive Male Infertility Management

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely treat idiopathic infertility with antioxidants, prebiotic/probiotic supplements, selective oestrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) or aromatase inhibitors (AIs).
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.2 Summary of evidence and recommendation for Non-Invasive Male Infertility Management

recommendations.statement: Use effective drug treatment—hCG, human menopausal gonadotropins, recombinant FSH or highly purified FSH—to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who want to conceive.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: Use FSH to increase spermatogenesis in men with idiopathic oligozoospermia whose FSH values are within the normal range.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: Do not treat idiopathic infertility with high dose FSH.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: Do not begin hormonal stimulation before TESE in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) outside clinical trials.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: Do not use testosterone therapy to treat male infertility.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: Provide testosterone therapy to symptomatic men with primary or secondary hypogonadism who are not planning parenthood.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: Offer dopamine agonist therapy to men with confirmed hyperprolactinemia to improve sperm quality.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: In infertile men using anabolic steroids, stop the steroids for six to twelve months before considering selective oestrogen receptor modulators or gonadotrophin therapy to induce spermatogenesis.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.5.3.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for treatment of male infertility with hormonal therapy

recommendations.statement: For azoospermia caused by vasal or epididymal obstruction, perform microsurgical vasovasostomy or epididymovasostomy when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.1.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for obstructive azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Use sperm retrieval methods such as microsurgical epididymal sperm aspiration (MESA), testicular sperm extraction (TESE), PESA or TESA alongside reconstructive surgery, when repair is not feasible, when the partner’s ovarian reserve is limited, or when the patient prefers to forgo reconstruction and proceed directly to ICSI.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.1.3 Summary of evidence and recommendations for obstructive azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Confirm non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) with two consecutive semen analyses showing no sperm after centrifugation.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: In patients with NOA, conduct a comprehensive assessment comprising a detailed medical history, hormonal profile, genetic testing and scrotal ultrasound to investigate the cause and associated comorbidity.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Ensure couples with genetic abnormalities receive genetic counselling before any assisted reproductive technology.
recommendations.context: Recommendation presented in the NOA section.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Perform surgical sperm retrieval in men with NOA who are candidates for assisted reproductive technology, such as ICSI.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Do not undertake surgical sperm retrieval in patients with complete AZFa and AZFb microdeletions.
recommendations.rationale: The chance of retrieving sperm is zero.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Do not use fine needle aspiration (FNA) or testicular sperm aspiration (TESA) in patients with NOA.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Do not use FNA mapping to predict the outcome before definitive testicular sperm extraction, regardless of extraction type, in patients with NOA.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Use microdissection TESE as the preferred method of sperm retrieval in patients with NOA.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Do not regard pre-operative biochemical and clinical variables as sufficiently reliable to predict surgical sperm retrieval outcomes in patients with NOA.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely administer medical therapy, such as hormonal stimulation, before c/mTESE to improve sperm retrieval in men with NOA and hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism.
recommendations.source_heading: 11.6.2.4 Recommendations for Non-Obstructive Azoospermia

conditions.name: Male infertility
conditions.description: A couple that is sexually active and does not use contraception is infertile when spontaneous pregnancy has not occurred within 12 months. Male-associated factors can impair fertility even when conventional semen parameters are normal.
conditions.epidemiology: About 15% of couples do not conceive within 12 consecutive months and seek care. A male-associated factor is identified in 50% of involuntarily childless couples; a solely male factor is identified in about 20% of infertile couples.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Potential contributors include urogenital or genetic abnormalities, malignancy, infection, varicocele, elevated scrotal temperature, endocrine or immunological disorders, prior procedures and gonadotoxic exposure. Advanced paternal age is an additional risk factor.

subtypes.name: Primary infertility
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The couple has never had a child and has not conceived after at least 12 consecutive months of intercourse without contraception.

subtypes.name: Secondary infertility
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The infertile couple has achieved pregnancy before, with the same or another partner.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify reproductive history, lifestyle and behavioural risks, systemic illness, infections, surgery, gonadotoxic medication and other exposures.
Assess secondary sexual characteristics, testes, epididymides, vasa deferentia, varicocele, penile abnormalities, body hair and gynaecomastia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Every infertile man, regardless of semen results.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Estimate testicular volume.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Reported mean volume is 20.0 ± 5.0 mL in the European general population and 18.0 ± 5.0 mL in infertile patients; measurements may exceed ultrasound estimates.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate semen volume and sperm number, motility and morphology using the WHO Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A single normal analysis is sufficient under WHO criteria. If the initial result is abnormal, obtain at least two consecutive analyses. No individual sperm parameter establishes infertility, and reference limits do not separate fertile from infertile men.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess endocrine causes of impaired fertility.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Part of the focused evaluation; serum total testosterone and Follicle Stimulating Hormone/Luteinising Hormone are indicated at least in oligozoospermia and azoospermia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate a possible genetic cause.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Selected according to clinical findings and semen parameters.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess testicular volume and structure, possible obstruction and lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Infertility assessment; particularly useful when orchidometry is unreliable.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of the female partner, including ovarian reserve
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform the timing and choice of fertility strategies.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In parallel with evaluation and management of the male partner.

long_term_effects: Increased risk of malignant and non-malignant conditions later in life.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Counselling and follow-up should account for later health risks and the possible psychological impact of infertility and unsuccessful treatment.

conditions.name: Idiopathic male infertility
conditions.description: This historical designation applies when no male-associated explanation is found for impaired sperm parameters despite an unremarkable relevant history, examination and endocrine, genetic and biochemical testing. Previously unrecognised environmental, oxidative, genetic or epigenetic factors may contribute.
conditions.epidemiology: No male-associated factor is found in 30-40% of cases with impaired sperm parameters.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Semen analysis may be abnormal despite otherwise normal clinical and laboratory findings.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify abnormalities in sperm parameters.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Findings can be pathological despite an otherwise unrevealing evaluation.

diagnostic_workup.test: Medical history, physical examination and endocrine, genetic and biochemical laboratory testing
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for an identifiable cause.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Evaluation of suspected idiopathic male infertility.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: These assessments are normal under the description of this entity.

conditions.name: Unexplained male infertility
conditions.description: Infertility remains of unknown origin despite normal sperm parameters and evaluation of the partner.
conditions.epidemiology: Between 20 and 30% of couples have unexplained infertility.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Conventional semen parameters are normal.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish whether conventional sperm parameters are normal.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Normal results do not establish fertility.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for an explanation in the partner.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The evaluation does not identify a cause.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess sperm DNA damage not captured by conventional semen analysis.

conditions.name: Oligozoospermia
conditions.description: Reduced sperm concentration; severe cases carry a higher incidence of genital-tract obstruction and genetic abnormalities.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Under the cited WHO 5th edition criteria, sperm concentration is < 16 million sperm/mL; severe oligozoospermia is described at spermatozoa < 5 million/mL.

subtypes.name: Severe oligozoospermia
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Spermatozoa < 5 million/mL; obstruction and genetic abnormalities occur more often.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Measure sperm concentration and other semen characteristics.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Under the cited WHO 5th edition criteria, oligozoospermia denotes < 16 million sperm/mL. Confirm an abnormal baseline result with at least two consecutive analyses.

diagnostic_workup.test: Serum total testosterone and Follicle Stimulating Hormone/Luteinising Hormone
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate endocrine function.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At least all cases of oligozoospermia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate chromosomal abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: The formal recommendation specifies spermatozoa < 5 million/mL; the diagnostic discussion also describes an indication at < 10 million/mL.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Patients with sperm count < 5 million/mL had a 10-fold higher incidence (4%) of mainly autosomal structural abnormalities than the general population.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify Y-chromosome deletions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Required at sperm concentrations ≤ 1 million sperm/mL; considered at < 5 million sperm/mL.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In the cited meta-analysis, most deletions occurred at ≤ 1 million sperm/mL, with < 1% identified above 1 million sperm/mL.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Testing is required at ≤ 1 million sperm/mL and considered at < 5 million sperm/mL.

conditions.name: Asthenozoospermia
conditions.description: A semen motility abnormality identified by a reduced proportion of progressively motile sperm under the cited WHO 5th edition criteria.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Progressively motile sperm are < 32% under the cited WHO 5th edition criteria.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Measure progressive sperm motility.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The cited WHO 5th edition threshold is < 32% progressive motile sperm; the WHO 6th edition does not report this subdivision, although the panel considers it clinically relevant.

conditions.name: Teratozoospermia
conditions.description: A sperm morphology abnormality defined using the cited WHO 5th edition criteria.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Normal sperm forms constitute < 4% under the cited WHO 5th edition criteria.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess sperm morphology.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The cited WHO 5th edition threshold is < 4% normal forms; the WHO 6th edition does not report this subdivision, although the panel considers it clinically relevant.

conditions.name: Oligo-astheno-terato-zoospermia (OAT) syndrome
conditions.description: The combined occurrence of reduced sperm concentration, progressive motility and normal morphology.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The three semen abnormalities occur together.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess sperm concentration, motility and morphology together.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: All three abnormalities are present.

conditions.name: Azoospermia
conditions.description: Complete absence of spermatozoa from semen; evaluation distinguishes an obstructive from a non-obstructive cause.
conditions.clinical_presentation: No spermatozoa are identified in the ejaculate.

subtypes.name: Obstructive azoospermia (OA)
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Absence of sperm results from an obstruction.

subtypes.name: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA)
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Absence of sperm accompanies severely impaired spermatogenesis or dysfunction of the hypothalamus-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis.

diagnostic_workup.test: At least two consecutive semen analyses
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm the absence of sperm.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An initially abnormal semen result requires confirmation.

diagnostic_workup.test: Semen centrifugation and microscopic examination of the pellet
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Distinguish absolute azoospermia from cryptozoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The described method uses 3,000 g for 15 minutes and phase-contrast microscopy at ×200 magnification; staining and repeat microscopy may identify small numbers of sperm.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Distinguish obstructive from non-obstructive azoospermia.

diagnostic_workup.test: Serum total testosterone and Follicle Stimulating Hormone/Luteinising Hormone
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess endocrine function.
Identify chromosomal abnormalities.

conditions.name: Obstructive azoospermia (OA)
conditions.description: Spermatozoa are absent from the sediment of centrifuged ejaculate because of an obstruction in the seminal tract.
conditions.epidemiology: Occurs in 20-40% of men with azoospermia.
conditions.clinical_presentation: FSH and testicular size are generally normal, and the epididymis may be enlarged. At least one testis may have a volume > 15 mL, although smaller testes can occur with concomitant partial testicular failure.

subtypes.name: Intratesticular obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The blockage is within the testis.

subtypes.name: Epididymal obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Potential causes include infection, trauma, prior surgery and congenital abnormalities.

subtypes.name: Vas deferens obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Potential causes include vasectomy, other surgery and congenital absence of the vas deferens.

subtypes.name: Ejaculatory duct obstruction (EDO)
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A distal obstruction that may be associated with cystic or post-inflammatory changes.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify previous procedures or injury and assess testicular volume, epididymal dilatation or nodules, and absence or atresia of the vas deferens.

diagnostic_workup.test: Semen analysis with examination of the centrifuged pellet
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm azoospermia and assess findings suggesting complete duct obstruction.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Absence of both spermatozoa and immature germ cells in the pellet suggests complete seminal-duct obstruction.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate low or absent semen volume.
Assess spermatogenic function.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Values should generally be normal in obstructive azoospermia but do not exclude other causes; inhibin-B offers no better diagnostic value than FSH.

diagnostic_workup.test: Cystic fibrose transmembrane conductance regulator gene testing
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate associated genetic abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Unilateral or bilateral absence of the vas deferens or seminal vesicle agenesis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the seminal tract and a suspected distal obstruction.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Low semen volume, acidic pH and severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia when obstruction is suspected.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Assessment is indicated with unilateral or bilateral vasal absence or seminal vesicle agenesis.

conditions.name: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA)
conditions.description: No sperm is found in the centrifuged ejaculate in the setting of a severe spermatogenic deficit, commonly related to primary testicular dysfunction or dysfunction of the hypothalamus-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. Ejaculate volume is usually normal.
conditions.epidemiology: Concomitant hypogonadism has been reported in about 30% of patients with NOA.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Testicular volume is often, but not always, reduced. NOA can be the first indication of a pituitary or testicular germ cell tumour.

diagnostic_workup.test: Two consecutive semen analyses with centrifugation
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm absence of sperm.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: No sperm is found after centrifugation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate possible causes and associated illness.
Identify and classify concomitant hypogonadism.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Distinguish hypogonadotropic, hypergonadotropic and compensated hypogonadism.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess testicular volume, dysgenesis, microcalcifications and possible tumour.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Routine Doppler assessment to predict surgical sperm retrieval is not supported by consistent data.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate chromosomal abnormalities.
Identify deletions relevant to diagnosis and sperm-retrieval prognosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Complete AZFa and AZFb microdeletions make sperm retrieval almost impossible.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess a possible alternative diagnosis associated with vasal absence.
Characterise spermatogenesis when tissue is obtained during therapeutic retrieval.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During a sperm-retrieval procedure, rather than as a separate diagnostic biopsy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Hypospermatogenesis has been associated with better retrieval prospects than maturation arrest or SCOS; no definitive pre-operative predictor has been established.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: A complete deletion involving AZFa is associated with a very poor prospect of surgical sperm retrieval.
A complete deletion involving AZFb is associated with a very poor prospect of surgical sperm retrieval.

follow_up.schedule: Long-term endocrine follow-up is reasonable after TESE.
long_term_effects: Increased risk of long-term cardio-metabolic disease, cancer and mortality.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The infertility assessment also offers an opportunity to evaluate longer-term comorbidity risks.

conditions.name: Klinefelter syndrome
conditions.description: A sex-chromosome abnormality associated with impaired fertility, variable sperm production and features of primary hypogonadism.
conditions.epidemiology: The document identifies it as the most common sex-chromosome abnormality.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Adults often have small, firm testes. Presentation ranges from otherwise normal virilisation to androgen-deficiency features; infertility and reduced testicular volume may be the only evident findings. Learning, language-processing or neuropsychological difficulties are often present.

subtypes.name: 46,XY/47,XX mosaicism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Germ cells and sperm production are observed more often than in non-mosaic Klinefelter syndrome.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify the sex-chromosome abnormality.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The described variants include 47,XXY and 46,XY/47, XX mosaicism.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess testicular size and sperm production.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Sperm production is variable.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify testosterone deficiency.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Deficiency is more frequent than in the general population.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Sex-chromosome pattern described for Klinefelter syndrome and associated infertility.
Mosaic variant in which sperm production is more frequently observed.

follow_up.schedule: Long-term endocrine and general medical follow-up is advised.
long_term_effects: Metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, including venous thromboembolism (VTE) and diabetes.
Reported higher risk of haematological malignancies.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Health risks require follow-up beyond fertility care, particularly when testosterone therapy is started.

conditions.name: Cystic fibrosis (CF)
conditions.description: An autosomal-recessive condition involving CFTR; associated reproductive-tract development may be affected.
conditions.epidemiology: The document reports that 4% of Caucasians carry mutations involving CFTR.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Men may have congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens; those with CBAVD can have mild clinical features such as a history of chest infections.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify a genetic explanation and inform reproductive counselling.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Structural absence of the vas deferens; testing of the partner is important when a man has CBAVD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: If the female partner carries a CFTR mutation, the stated risk of a child with CF or CBAVD is 50%, depending on parental mutations; if she tests negative for known mutations, the stated risk of carrying an unknown mutation is ~0.4%.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Alterations may cause CBAVD; the document states that only homozygous mutations exhibit CF disease.
Named among the most frequently found mutations, with frequency dependent on ethnicity.
Named among the most frequently found mutations, with frequency dependent on ethnicity.
Named among the most frequently found mutations, with frequency dependent on ethnicity.
Considered a mild CFTR mutation rather than a polymorphism.

conditions.name: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD)
conditions.description: Congenital absence of both vasa deferentia associated with CFTR alterations and obstructive azoospermia.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported in 1% of infertile men and in up to 6% of men with obstructive azoospermia.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Absent vasa can be overlooked on examination; semen volume may be < 1.0 mL with acidic pH < 7.0. Some men have mild features of CF.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify congenital absence.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: All men with azoospermia, particularly with semen volume < 1.0 mL and pH < 7.0.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Absence of the vasa supports CBAVD.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify findings that raise suspicion of CBAVD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Volume < 1.0 mL and acidic pH < 7.0 are highlighted.

diagnostic_workup.test: CFTR mutation testing, including 5T allele analysis
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate genetic cause and reproductive risk.

diagnostic_workup.test: CFTR mutation testing of the female partner
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform counselling about potential transmission.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When the male partner has CBAVD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: If the partner carries a mutation, the stated risk of a child with CF or CBAVD is 50%, depending on the parental mutations.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the epididymis and seminal vesicles and other structural findings.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Described epididymal appearances include tubular ectasia, a meshwork pattern and partial or complete absence.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess renal and other abdominal anomalies.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Bilateral absence of the vas deferens without CFTR mutations.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Alterations may underlie CBAVD and affect reproductive counselling.
The document considers this variant a mild CFTR mutation.

conditions.name: Congenital unilateral absence of the vas deferens (CUAVD)
conditions.description: Congenital absence of one vas deferens, usually associated with absence of the kidney on the same side.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Unilateral vasal absence may occur with an ipsilateral renal abnormality.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify unilateral absence.
Investigate an associated genetic alteration.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Unilateral absence of the vas deferens with normal kidneys.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess renal abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Unilateral absence of the vas deferens without CFTR mutations.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Possible findings include ipsilateral renal absence or other renal abnormalities.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Screening is indicated for unilateral vasal absence with normal kidneys.

conditions.name: Y microdeletions
conditions.description: Partial or complete deletions affecting Y-chromosome AZF regions are a molecular genetic cause of severe oligozoospermia and azoospermia.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported frequency is 8-12% among azoospermic men and 3-7% among oligozoospermic men; at sperm concentrations > 5 million/mL, deletions are reported at ~0.7%. AZFc accounts for 65-70%, AZFb and AZFb+c or AZFa+b+c for 25-30%, and AZFa for 5%.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The phenotype varies by deletion and may include severe impairment or absence of spermatogenesis.

subtypes.name: AZFa
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Complete deletion is associated with Sertoli cell only syndrome [SCOS] and poor prospects for surgical sperm retrieval.

subtypes.name: AZFb
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Complete deletion is associated with spermatogenic arrest and poor prospects for surgical sperm retrieval.

subtypes.name: AZFc
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The phenotype ranges from oligozoospermia to azoospermia; testicular sperm can be found in 50-75% of affected men.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Determine sperm concentration for assessment and testing decisions.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Y-deletions are uncommon when sperm concentration exceeds 5 million/mL.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify the deletion and inform diagnosis and sperm-retrieval prognosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Required when sperm concentration is ≤ 1 million sperm/mL; considered when it is < 5 million sperm/mL.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Complete deletions involving AZFa and AZFb have a very poor surgical sperm-retrieval prognosis; male offspring of men with AZF microdeletions inherit the deletion.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Complete deletion is associated with SCOS and a poor surgical sperm-retrieval prognosis.
Complete deletion is associated with spermatogenic arrest and a poor surgical sperm-retrieval prognosis.
Phenotype varies; testicular sperm can be found in 50-75% of affected men, and sons inherit the deletion.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: Genetic counselling should address transmission to sons before ICSI.

conditions.name: Cryptorchidism
conditions.description: A testis that has not reached or remained in the scrotum; the adult management addressed by this guideline depends on laterality, location, testicular function and malignancy risk.
conditions.epidemiology: At 1 year of age, nearly 1% of full-term male infants have cryptorchidism; approximately 30% of undescended testes are nonpalpable. A history of cryptorchidism is present in 5-10% of testicular cancers. Germ cell tumour risk is 3.6-7.4 times that of the general population, and 2-6% of affected men develop a testicular tumour.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Testes may be unilateral or bilateral and inguinal, intra-abdominal or ectopic. Men can have impaired semen parameters, reduced testicular volume or hormonal dysfunction.

subtypes.name: Congenital cryptorchidism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The undescended testis was identified from birth.

subtypes.name: Acquired cryptorchidism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The testis was previously situated in the scrotum.

subtypes.name: Unilateral cryptorchidism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: One testis is undescended; the contralateral descended testis may also show structural or fertility-related abnormalities.

subtypes.name: Bilateral cryptorchidism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Both testes are affected, with greater adverse effects on testicular volume, hormonal function and fertility than unilateral disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Determine location, palpability, laterality and testicular characteristics.
Assess impaired sperm production and fertility.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Adult evaluation, particularly when fertility preservation is relevant.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In outcome studies, untreated bilateral undescended testes were associated with oligospermia in 100% and azoospermia in 75%; following successful bilateral treatment, the reported figures were 75% and 42%, respectively.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate testicular function and a possible long-term consequence.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: History of cryptorchidism, particularly when deciding adult management.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Exclude intratubular germ cell neoplasia in situ (GCNIS).
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At adult orchidopexy of an undescended testis.

follow_up.schedule: Regular testicular self-examination is advised for men with a history of cryptorchidism.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Counsel patients about cancer risk even after early orchidopexy.

conditions.name: Testicular germ cell tumour (TGCT)
conditions.description: A testicular malignancy relevant to fertility before and after oncological treatment; seminomas and nonseminomas are generally preceded by GCNIS.
conditions.epidemiology: It affects approximately 1% of sub-fertile men. The document reports an average 10-year survival rate for testicular cancer of 98%; among men with TGCT, azoospermia was observed in 24% and oligospermia in 50% before treatment.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Semen quality may already be impaired at diagnosis. Leydig cell dysfunction can involve the contralateral testis.

subtypes.name: Seminomas
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Generally preceded by GCNIS.

subtypes.name: Nonseminomas
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Generally preceded by GCNIS.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify azoospermia or marked semen abnormalities and inform fertility preservation.
Assess testicular lesions and the contralateral testis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Assessment of suspected or identified testicular abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Ultrasound alone cannot reliably classify many lesions as benign or malignant.

diagnostic_workup.test: Pre-treatment testosterone, SHBG, LH and oestradiol
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish a baseline and assess risk of subsequent hypogonadism.
Evaluate hypogonadism during subsequent care.
Assess for GCNIS.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At orchidectomy in patients at high risk, including a history of cryptorchidism, testicular volume < 12 mL or poor spermatogenesis.

follow_up.schedule: Long-term multidisciplinary survivorship care is advised; the document does not specify visit intervals.
recommended_tests: Monitoring for sexual dysfunction and cardiovascular risk.
long_term_effects: Impaired semen quality and possible infertility after treatment.
Sperm aneuploidy and increased SDF after gonadotoxic treatment.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Survivorship care should incorporate psychological, medical and social needs. The risk of hypogonadism is greatest at 6-12 months after treatment; spermatogenesis usually recovers one to four years after chemotherapy.

conditions.name: Testicular microcalcification (TM)
conditions.description: An ultrasound finding within the testicular parenchyma that can occur with benign conditions as well as GCNIS or TGCT. The calcification itself is not malignant, and its association with future cancer remains clinically complex.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported in 0.6-9% of men referred for testicular US and in 6-46% of men with TGCT. A cited meta-analysis of infertile men reported an association with testicular cancer of pooled OR: 18.11, 95% CI: 8.09, 40.55; p < 0.0001. In a cited 5-year follow-up, testicular cancer did not develop in 98.4% of men with TM.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Often detected on imaging. Additional factors relevant to malignancy assessment include infertility, bilateral TM, testicular atrophy, undescended testes and a history of TGCT.

subtypes.name: Isolated TM
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Microcalcification without associated risk factors or suspicious lesions.

subtypes.name: Bilateral TM
